unit.why: An anecdote about R. Shmelke of Nikolsburg arriving at his rabbinate and addressing himself with honorifics, followed by the author's long homiletic expansion.

stories.start_quote: מעשה מרב האי גאון קדוש ה׳
stories.end_quote: זה נאמר בעבודת ד' וזה במסחר וקנין
stories.summary_en: When R. Shmelke arrived to take up the rabbinate of Nikolsburg amid great honours, he loudly addressed himself as 'Rabbi Reb Shmelke'. Asked why by a learned rich man, he explained that the honour others give should be as worthless to him as honour he gives himself, and the townspeople recognised him as a holy tzaddik. The author then adds a homily reconciling this with R. Eliezer's charge to beware of a fellow's honour.

quotes: ככה צריך להיות כל כבוד המדומה של אנשים
שנעבדו את ד' בלי שום גאות ופניות
tags.why: The point is contempt for honour, i.e. humility.

quotes: בעיני העם מוזר הדברים אלה עד מאוד
tags.why: His behaviour looks like pursuit of honour, and the lesson rejects pride.
The anecdote illustrates the tzaddik's humility.

quotes: כאשר נתכהן הגאון הקדוש הנזכר לשרת בקודש
tags.why: His installation and reception as rabbi of the community is the setting.

quotes: ותיכף ראו כולמו לדעת כי צדיק קדוש עליון הוא
tags.why: The puzzled people realise his strange conduct reveals holiness.

quotes: זה הפי' ממאמרם ז"ל יהי כבוד חבירך חביב עליך כשלך
tags.why: The tzaddik explains a rabbinic dictum as his teaching.
The anecdote is wrapped in an extended homily by the author on R. Eliezer's saying.

quotes: לקול תרועת ששון ועליצות לב כל אחד
tags.why: The community rejoices at his arrival.
The text gives moral instruction about honour.
